alalal-e86942-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 6: on the number of articles in each creed.

alalal-e86942-d1e113.summary: States the third problem: the number of articles according to both creeds, the Nicene and the Apostles'.

alalal-e86942-d1e122.summary: Introduces objections that the number falls short of the articles in the Athanasian Creed.

alalal-e86942-d1e132.summary: First objection: omniscience and divine goodness are divine properties like omnipotence, yet only omnipotence is an article.

alalal-e86942-d1e143.summary: Second objection: the Athanasian Creed calls each person omnipotent, immense and uncreated, but only omnipotence appears among the articles.

alalal-e86942-d1e168.summary: Third objection: the Athanasian Creed also says each person is Lord.

alalal-e86942-d1e178.summary: Fourth objection: there should be an article on the personal properties by which the persons are distinguished, but neither creed has one.

alalal-e86942-d1e198.summary: Fifth objection: there were many errors on the union of natures in Christ (confusion, mixture, conversion), and articles exclude errors, so there should be more articles on the mode of union.

alalal-e86942-d1e218.summary: Sixth objection: the Apostles' Creed has one article 'I believe in God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth', which the Nicene divides in two; if it is an indivisible truth it should not be divided, so one creed errs.

alalal-e86942-d1e264.summary: Seventh objection: the Apostles' Creed has one article on conception and birth, which the Nicene divides into two.

alalal-e86942-d1e285.summary: Eighth objection: if the nativity is divided for its two births, in and from the womb, the passion should be divided into five (capture, mockery, suffering, death, burial), yet both creeds keep it as one.

alalal-e86942-d1e307.summary: Ninth objection: the Nicene Creed omits the descent into hell, and Anselm says it does not contain the faith entire, so it is deficient.

alalal-e86942-d1e327.summary: Tenth objection: one division counts descent and resurrection as two articles, the Apostles' Creed as one, so one division is invalid.

alalal-e86942-d1e340.summary: Eleventh objection: the Apostles' Creed has 'the holy Church' and 'the communion of saints' as two articles, while the Nicene joins 'one holy catholic and apostolic Church' and 'one baptism for the remission of sins' into one; by what right did the Apostles divide them?

alalal-e86942-d1e373.summary: Twelfth objection: since there is an article on eternal life and we also believe in eternal punishment, there should be one on eternal punishment.

alalal-e86942-d1e387.summary: Thirteenth objection: Cassian and Leo cite a third creed, of the Synod of Antioch, with content found in neither of the others, such as 'the one and only true God' and 'firstborn of every creature'.

alalal-e86942-d1e440.summary: Fourteenth objection: the Antiochene creed adds 'firstborn of every creature' in the third article, found in neither other creed, so both are deficient.

alalal-e86942-d1e460.summary: Fifteenth objection: since the Apostles composed their creed, every preacher of faith should have added a sentence, but nothing comes from Paul and Barnabas, though chosen by the Spirit.

alalal-e86942-d1e480.summary: Sixteenth objection, on individual articles: 'I believe in one God' is not a necessary article, since philosophers such as Aristotle and Avicenna proved it by necessary reasons.

alalal-e86942-d1e500.summary: Seventeenth: why not 'one simple God', since simplicity is more proper to God than unity?

alalal-e86942-d1e511.summary: Eighteenth: omnipotence is common to the three, so 'Father almighty' could occasion error.

alalal-e86942-d1e533.summary: Nineteenth: why does the Nicene say 'maker' where the Antiochene says 'creator', since creating suits omnipotence better?

alalal-e86942-d1e551.summary: Twentieth, on the third article: Christ is not the only Lord, since the Athanasian Creed calls each person Lord.

alalal-e86942-d1e570.summary: Twenty-first: the many expansions in this article ('only-begotten, born of the Father before all ages, God from God, light from light, true God from true God, begotten not made, consubstantial') seem superfluous once 'Son of God' is said.

alalal-e86942-d1e610.summary: Twenty-second: 'for us men and for our salvation' seems redundant.

alalal-e86942-d1e637.summary: Twenty-third: 'descended' and 'was incarnate' seem the same, since the descent was not local but appearing visibly in flesh.

alalal-e86942-d1e653.summary: Twenty-fourth: 'and was made man' seems to add nothing, since being incarnate and becoming man are the same.

alalal-e86942-d1e670.summary: But if it is not a distinct article, the Nicene Creed would lack the article on Christ's birth, which all count among the seven attributed to the Son.

alalal-e86942-d1e686.summary: Twenty-fifth: on 'crucified for us... and buried', asks why the Nicene and Antiochene creeds lack the descent into hell while the Apostles' Creed has it.

alalal-e86942-d1e711.summary: Twenty-sixth: why is nothing said of the many appearances between resurrection and ascension, which Paul in 1 Corinthians 15 seems to include among what he handed on?

alalal-e86942-d1e757.summary: Twenty-seventh: the coming to judgment seems to belong neither to nature nor to glory but to severity, so it should not be an article.

alalal-e86942-d1e778.summary: Twenty-eighth: why such elaboration about the Holy Spirit, called Lord and life-giver, with his procession, equal worship and speaking through the prophets?

alalal-e86942-d1e799.summary: Twenty-ninth: why do the Nicene Fathers join the two Apostles' articles of Matthew (holy Church) and Simon (communion of saints) into one, adding 'I confess one baptism for the remission of sins'? The Fathers did not do this without cause.

alalal-e86942-d1e832.summary: Solution begins: the Apostles' Creed has twelve articles by the number of Apostles who contributed, figured by the twelve oxen under the bronze sea and the twelve stones taken from the Jordan where the ark stood; the stones are the articles for their solidity, the ark Christ, the Jordan the Old Testament, the priests the lawgivers, prophets and patriarchs grounded on the articles, so that the New is a wheel within the wheel of the Old.
claims: The Apostles' Creed has twelve articles corresponding to the twelve Apostles.

alalal-e86942-d1e897.summary: The traditional distribution: the first article, attributed to the Father and contributed by Peter, is 'I believe in God the Father almighty, creator...'.

alalal-e86942-d1e913.summary: Six articles are attributed to the Son.

alalal-e86942-d1e918.summary: The first concerns his divine generation, contributed by Andrew: 'And in Jesus Christ his only Son our Lord'.

alalal-e86942-d1e932.summary: The second concerns both human births, in and from the womb, contributed by John, guardian of the Mother: 'conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary'.

alalal-e86942-d1e951.summary: The third concerns the mystery of the passion with all surrounding his death, suffering, death and burial, contributed by James, brother of John: 'suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died and was buried'.

alalal-e86942-d1e977.summary: The fourth concerns the redemption of those in limbo (Zechariah 9:11), contributed by Thomas: 'descended into hell, rose again from the dead'. Descent and resurrection are joined because together they express all Christ merited by his death: the soul's redemption in harrowing hell (Psalm 106) and the body's in the glorious resurrection (Philippians 3:21), since man is fully redeemed only in body and soul. Thomas fittingly contributed it, having touched the wounds and confessed 'my Lord and my God'.
claims: Descent and resurrection form one article expressing redemption of soul and body.

alalal-e86942-d1e1061.summary: The fifth concerns the opening of the place of beatitude, where Jesus entered as forerunner, contributed by James the Less: 'ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of God the Father almighty', expressing the place, Christ's possession of the highest goods in his humanity, and his equality in divinity.

alalal-e86942-d1e1105.summary: The sixth concerns the return to judgment, since the Father has given all judgment to the Son, so that he who gave the law and was judged for the living and dead judges them; contributed by Philip: 'from thence he will come to judge the living and the dead'.

alalal-e86942-d1e1130.summary: The remaining five concern the Holy Spirit in himself and in his gifts; the first, expressing his personhood, contributed by Bartholomew: 'I believe in the Holy Spirit'.

alalal-e86942-d1e1149.summary: The first of the gifts is the sanctifying and uniting of the Church, contributed by Matthew, who experienced it when changed from publican to evangelist: 'the holy catholic Church', meaning the Spirit sanctifying the universal Church, universal (Boethius) because preached throughout the world and holding universally true articles.

alalal-e86942-d1e1194.summary: The next is the effect of grace against sin, contributed by Simon the Canaanite: 'the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins'. The communion of goods comes only through the Spirit uniting and vivifying the mystical body, and requires removal of what is purely one's own, sin; so the two are joined, since once sin is removed only communion remains.
claims: The communion of saints and forgiveness of sins form one article, since removal of sin leaves communion.

alalal-e86942-d1e1248.summary: The next concerns the Spirit breathing on those poisoned by the serpent (Ezekiel), contributed by Jude Thaddeus: 'the resurrection of the flesh', meaning the Spirit causing the resurrection by sending the created spirit into the body.

alalal-e86942-d1e1273.summary: The last, 'life everlasting, amen', was contributed by Matthias, last elected, meaning the Spirit's goodness rewarding the saints with eternal life, since he is the life-giver.

alalal-e86942-d1e1292.summary: Another division, of the doctors following the Nicene Creed, counts fourteen articles, two of which, birth from the womb and the descent into hell, are contained only implicitly. Seven concern the divinity and seven the divinity in the humanity, figured by the seven stars and seven golden lampstands of Apocalypse 1.
claims: The Nicene division counts fourteen articles: seven on the divinity, seven on the incarnation.

alalal-e86942-d1e1338.summary: Derives the seven articles on the divinity: God is known by essence, in persons and in effects. By essence, 'I believe in one God'. The Father, never sent, is known only through his appropriated work, omnipotence and creation from nothing: 'Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth'. The Son, sent and knowable in effect: 'in one Lord Jesus Christ... consubstantial with the Father'. The Holy Spirit: 'Lord and life-giver, proceeding from the Father and the Son...'. Effects belonging to human reformation are three: re-creation of the soul by grace, 'one holy apostolic Church... one baptism'; the glory of the flesh, 'the resurrection of the dead'; and what follows both, 'the life of the world to come'.
claims: The seven articles on the divinity follow from knowing God by essence, in three persons, and in three saving effects.

alalal-e86942-d1e1494.summary: Derives the seven articles on the incarnation, divided into Christ's merit and its effect. Merit: entry into the state of meriting by the union of natures, 'descended... was incarnate'; and by the birth from the womb and his human life, 'and was made man', called by masters 'born of the Virgin Mary'; and the noblest act of satisfaction, 'crucified... suffered and was buried'. Effect: the robe of glory, by the term from which he redeemed (hell, by resurrection), the term to which (life, in the risen head), and the recovery of the place, 'ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand'; and judicial power merited by being judged, 'will come again in glory to judge... whose kingdom will have no end'.
claims: The seven articles on the incarnation divide into those of Christ's merit and those of its effects.

alalal-e86942-d1e1651.summary: Turns to answering the objections in order.

alalal-e86942-d1e1659.summary: Reply to the first: to the Father is attributed what is appropriated to his person and its act, since otherwise he would not be knowable, not being sent; omniscience and goodness do not so express divinity, since omniscience was given to Christ's soul but not omnipotence, and goodness is not 'omni-' in the same way. Another answer, that omnipotence alone is shown by one act, creation, is rejected, since omnipotence is an article only as the Father's attribute.
claims: Omnipotence is an article as appropriated to the Father, through whom he is known since he is not sent.

alalal-e86942-d1e1703.summary: Reply to the second: 'immense', 'uncreated' and the like explain the unity of the persons in essence, as Athanasius intends; explanation does not make an article, since it is presupposed in what it explains.

alalal-e86942-d1e1721.summary: Reply to the third: 'Lord' is said at Nicaea of the Son and the Spirit, against Arius, who made the Son a creature, and against those who made the Spirit a servant; since no one doubted the Father's lordship, it was understood, and Athanasius made it explicit.

alalal-e86942-d1e1758.summary: Reply to the fourth: divine properties are not distinct from the persons but are the persons; there is no further real distinction, so there should be no special article on them, lest the persons seem composite.
claims: Personal properties are identical with the persons and need no separate article.

alalal-e86942-d1e1782.summary: Reply to the fifth: there is one article on the mode of union, since the union is in one way only, natures preserved in one person, expressed by 'was incarnate'; as virtue, lying in one mean, excludes many vices, faith by one confession excludes every heresy, being the mean between heresies (Boethius); Athanasius expounded this at length.
claims: One article on the union excludes all Christological heresies, as faith is the mean between heresies.

alalal-e86942-d1e1824.summary: Reply to the sixth: the Apostles fitted their creed to their own number, not to the number of credibles, so they sometimes joined what was divisible and sometimes divided. Alternatively, the Father is principle both of creation and of the whole divinity, to whom unity is attributed, so Peter joined his article with essential principle and unity.

alalal-e86942-d1e1862.summary: Reply to the seventh: some things joined in the Apostles' Creed later had to be divided because of heresies: the Manichees said Christ was not truly born or made man but appeared in phantasm, and others that he was truly born but not conceived, bringing his body from heaven; so the Fathers divided conception from becoming man, which was unnecessary before heresies arose.
claims: Articles were divided in the Nicene Creed to exclude later heresies.

alalal-e86942-d1e1901.summary: Reply to the eighth: the passion need not be divided, since its five elements are ordered to the death and occurred in a brief continuous time, unlike conception and birth; and, the stronger reason, no heresy pressed, since the only one about Christ's death was the Manichaean claim that he suffered and died only in appearance.

alalal-e86942-d1e1936.summary: Reply to the ninth: Innocent explains that the Nicene Creed left the descent implicit because an error was spreading that Christ descended and did not return, so the Fathers suppressed it by including the descent in the resurrection, since if he rose his soul returned from hell. Some, citing Gregory, say it was still doubtful whether it was a separate article, since John had doubted whether Christ would descend himself; Albert thinks this unsafe to say.
claims: The Nicene Creed contains the descent into hell implicitly within the resurrection.

alalal-e86942-d1e1986.summary: On Anselm: he means the Nicene Creed does not contain the faith sufficiently explicitly, though it contains it implicitly.

alalal-e86942-d1e1997.summary: Reply to the tenth: both are valid under two views of resurrection: as a motion, descent gives its terminus from which, so they form one; as things done to Christ, they are two, as the doctors count them.

alalal-e86942-d1e2026.summary: Reply to the eleventh: the Apostles divided according to the acts of grace, sanctifying the Church and sharing goods by remitting sins; the Fathers joined them considering the unity of the Spirit's grace in substance; both are reasonable.

alalal-e86942-d1e2049.summary: Reply to the twelfth: punishments are believed by opposition, since if God rewards he will by the same justice punish the wicked; but there is no special article, since faith does not move toward this but away from it. On the Antiochene creed: it was not promulgated like the other two, since 'only true God' could suggest solitude in God excluding the plurality of persons, so this was removed at Nicaea.
claims: Eternal punishment is believed by implication from reward, not as a separate article.

alalal-e86942-d1e2088.summary: Reply to the fourteenth: 'firstborn of every creature' is true when soundly understood, as Basil says, receiving being being common with creatures and having it by nature proper to the Son; but it suggested Arius' heresy to the simple and so was removed at Nicaea.

alalal-e86942-d1e2117.summary: Reply to the fifteenth: Paul and Barnabas were chosen after the Creed was composed (Acts 13:2), so they added nothing.

alalal-e86942-d1e2133.summary: Reply to the sixteenth: 'one God' is an article not as proved but as held by the faithful, which means saying how he is one, a unity compatible with the Trinity; no philosopher understood this, since they proved unity scientifically, that it is, not what that one is.
claims: The article of one God concerns a unity compatible with the Trinity, which philosophy never reached.

alalal-e86942-d1e2157.summary: Reply to the seventeenth: simplicity is included in unity, since, as Boethius says, the truly one is that in which there is no number and which rests on nothing else; only the simple is one in this way.

alalal-e86942-d1e2173.summary: Reply to the eighteenth: omnipotence is appropriated to the Father and creation is the act manifesting it, since he is not sent; no error follows, since the Father, communicating his substance, communicates the same power, as the Creed implies with 'consubstantial' and the Spirit's co-adoration.

alalal-e86942-d1e2205.summary: Reply to the nineteenth: 'maker' was chosen wisely against heretical philosophers who said God created the world in its first principles and left its making to angels or nature; since heaven can be made only by creation from nothing, having no prior matter, 'maker of heaven' implies creation, and the verb implies he also makes all that is formed from the matter he created.
claims: 'Maker of heaven and earth' implies both creation from nothing and God's making of all things formed from matter.

alalal-e86942-d1e2247.summary: Reply to the twentieth: answered above in the third argument.

alalal-e86942-d1e2254.summary: Reply to the twenty-first: all those expressions were directed against Arius: 'one Lord' against his making the Son a creature; 'only-begotten, light from light' against denying co-eternity; 'true God from true God' against calling him God by adoption; 'begotten not made' against 'made'; 'consubstantial' against difference of substance; 'through whom all things were made' against denying his eternal co-operation; so that the people could not be deceived by Arians.
claims: The Nicene expansions on the Son each exclude a specific Arian error.

alalal-e86942-d1e2315.summary: Reply to the twenty-second: 'for us men' signifies love of conformity of nature with us, against the Manichee; 'for our salvation' signifies the effect of the redemption accomplished through him.

alalal-e86942-d1e2341.summary: Reply to the twenty-third: 'descended' implies incarnation only when understood in a catholic sense, which is not enough against heretics: Paul of Samosata said he was incarnate but did not descend, being a mere man; the Manichee that he descended but did not take our flesh; so both had to be expressed.

alalal-e86942-d1e2370.summary: Reply to the twenty-fourth: 'was made man' expresses the article of birth from the womb, when he began to be a man by himself, and includes all he did until the passion. Against those who exclude his life's acts from the articles, Albert holds that baptism and all by which he founded faith and planted the Church in the Apostles are reduced by the Fathers to 'and was made man', which is why they did not speak only of the birth, which expresses only one mystery.
claims: 'And was made man' includes the nativity and all the acts of Christ's life by which he founded the Church.

alalal-e86942-d1e2427.summary: Reply to the twenty-fifth: answered by Innocent's explanation above.

alalal-e86942-d1e2434.summary: Reply to the twenty-sixth: the appearances are proof of the resurrection, so they are not a special credible but are presupposed with the resurrection as proving it.

alalal-e86942-d1e2445.summary: Reply to the twenty-seventh: the coming to judgment belongs to grace, since the just will be rewarded there, the end of all grace, and by opposition the wicked punished for neglecting grace; as opposites fall under one discipline, one is understood in the other.

alalal-e86942-d1e2465.summary: Reply to the twenty-eighth: the expressions about the Spirit were made against those who made him a servant of Father and Son, a power alien to their essence, not giving life or inspiration; hence 'Lord and life-giver', and for co-essentiality 'who proceeds from the Father and the Son, who with them is adored and glorified'; and against Montanus and Porphyry, who said the prophets spoke like the possessed, 'who spoke through the prophets'.

alalal-e86942-d1e2522.summary: Reply to the last: as said, it is due to different considerations of grace, by substance one article, by acts several.

alalal-e86942.summary: Article 6 treats the number of articles in the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds against twenty-nine objections. These concern apparent omissions relative to the Athanasian and Antiochene creeds, the different ways the creeds divide the articles, the descent into hell, and the wording of the Nicene articles. Albert gives the traditional division of the Apostles' Creed into twelve articles, one per Apostle, prefigured by the twelve stones from the Jordan. One article belongs to the Father, six to the Son and five to the Holy Spirit, each assigned to its Apostle with a rationale. He then derives the doctors' fourteen-article Nicene division. Seven articles concern the divinity, known by essence, in three persons, and in three saving effects. Seven concern the incarnation, divided into Christ's merit and its effects. The replies explain that articles were joined or divided according to the number of the Apostles and the needs of refuting heresy. Omnipotence is an article as the Father's appropriated attribute. Personal properties are the persons themselves. One article on the union excludes every Christological heresy. The descent into hell is implicit in the Nicene resurrection. Eternal punishment is believed through the article on reward. Nearly every Nicene expansion excludes a specific Arian, Manichaean or pneumatological error, and 'and was made man' covers the mysteries of Christ's life.
claims: The Apostles' Creed has twelve articles, one per Apostle; the Nicene division counts fourteen, seven on the divinity and seven on the incarnation.
Articles were joined or divided according to apostolic number and the need to exclude heresies.
The Nicene expansions on the Son and the Spirit each exclude specific heresies.
Some truths, such as the descent into hell, eternal punishment and personal properties, are contained implicitly rather than as separate articles.
